**Yes, some can, but only models that document a UPS or EPS mode with automatic switchover.** A basic power station may keep a computer running but still cut power for a moment during an outage, and that can reboot the PC ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).

**What to check**
- **Switchover time:** 10 ms is the best you'll see on these models. Anker notes that 10 or 20 ms is fast but not 0 ms, and says that if a device manual requires 0 ms, an online double-conversion UPS is safer ([Anker NAS/UPS guide](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). Most desktop and laptop power supplies tolerate short gaps, but check yours, because none of the sources confirm this for specific PCs.
- **Pass-through:** Confirm the model supports running from the wall while charging.
- **Output and capacity:** Your PC's wattage must fit under the station's continuous output rating. Runtime is roughly Wh × 0.85 ÷ load in watts.
- **Waveform:** Pure sine wave output is preferred for computers.

**Models with a listed UPS switchover time**
- **Budget, laptop or small PC:** [BLUETTI Elite 30 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2) has ≤10 ms, 288 Wh and 600 W. It's $289.99, or $275.50 with code AFF5OFF. The small battery only covers short runtimes.
- **More capacity:** [ALLPOWERS P1800](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh) has 1,024 Wh and 1,800 W. It's $439, or $395.10 with code ALLPOWERS26. The listing says ≤10 ms, but the product images say 15 ms, and the store page contradicts itself on some specs. Verify before buying.
- **Desktop plus router and more:** [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) has ≤15 ms, 2,073.6 Wh and 2,600 W. It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF.
- **Anker SOLIX S2000:** It has 10 ms, 2,010 Wh and 1,500 W pure sine wave output, and costs $699.99 after coupon ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)). I only have Anker's blog page, not a product link.
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus:** EcoFlow says it has under 10 ms and 600 W output ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). I don't have pricing or a buy link for it.

I'd avoid the BLUETTI AC180 and AC200L at 20 ms if your PC is sensitive to power gaps. EcoFlow's claim that most stations "damage devices" is a manufacturer's marketing position, so weigh it accordingly.

**Bottom line:** For a typical home PC, a 10 ms station is a reasonable choice. For critical data, servers or NAS, or a power supply that needs 0 ms, buy a dedicated online UPS instead.

Dealectric's buy links are affiliate links, so they get paid if you buy, at no cost to you ([source](https://dealectric.com/answers/portable-power-station-ups-transfer-time-computer-manufacturer-guidance-ecoflow-)). Discount codes were last tested around Oct 21–24, 2026.

If you tell me your computer's wattage and how long you want it to run, I can narrow this down.
